title: staggered-queue-hang-caused-by-admission-token-staleness-in-scheduler-snapshot-path
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted and Dedicated reported intermittent large spikes of short-request latency and a subset of requests entering a hung state for several seconds during mixed-length traffic patterns. Investigation shows the batching/scheduler admission path can hold stale admission tokens after a scheduler snapshot update, preventing short requests from forming preemptive batches and causing queue build-up. This appears only under mixed workloads and when snapshot updates coincide with inflight admission holders. Private (on-prem) customers saw similar symptoms when their upgrade/maintenance windows triggered scheduler state rotation.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy two synthetic clients: one producing many short (<=32 tokens) requests, another sporadically submitting long (>=2048 tokens) requests to the same tenant.
2) Configure continuous-batching with default admission token TTL and enable scheduler snapshot rotation every ~30s in test cluster.
3) Start long request client to create large in-flight KV/cache state, then trigger a scheduler snapshot update (simulate host maintenance or config push).
4) Observe short requests stop forming low-latency batches for ~1-10s while the admission token(s) held by the long requests are not released; metric queue_length and per-tenant mean_latency spike.
5) Reproduce reliably by tuning snapshot frequency and mixing request ratios; failure more likely under high tenant density on a host.
telemetry_summary: Trace aggregation shows a cluster of requests with admission_token_acquired but no corresponding token_release event after scheduler_snapshot_change. Token holder goroutine remained parked waiting on preempt path that never executed due to a race: snapshot invalidation cleared preempt flag but did not clear inbound hold list. Metrics: tenant_queue_length +430% during incident window; p50 short-request latency from 12ms -> 380ms; tail p99 spikes up to 6.2s in worst repro. Affected tenants span hosted customers and 2 dedicated clusters; private customers reported similar behavior tied to upgrade windows.
triage_notes: 2026-03-01: Triage call with SRE, Runtime, and PM. Pattern looks like admission lifecycle bug introduced in snapshot rotation refactor (runtime-1.18->1.19).
2026-03-02: Correlated errors with scheduler_snapshot.version churn around customer escalations. No evidence of OOM or kernel saturation.
2026-03-03: Reproducer built; confirms race between snapshot invalidate and admission release path under mixed-length workloads.
2026-03-04: Customer comms drafted; mitigating guidance created for Dedicated/Private operators (temporary throttle of snapshot rotation and increase admission TTL).
mitigation_plan: Hotfix: add explicit token_release on snapshot_invalidate path to ensure held admissions are cleared within 250ms.
Introduce admission_watchdog: background walker that forces a soft-preempt if tokens show no progress for >500ms.
Configuration change for affected Dedicated/Private clusters: set scheduler.snapshot_rotation_interval to 5m and admission_token_ttl to 3s (temporary).
Customer-facing mitigation: instruct hosted customers to enable 'short-request-priority' flag to bias preemption while patch is rolled out.
Short-term rollout: push hotfix to Hosted canary (5%), run synthetic repro tests, promote to 25% then 100% if stable.
Dedicated/Private: provide patch bundles and upgrade instructions, coordinate maintenance windows with customers.
rollout_plan: Canary 5% (hosted) with synthetic mixed-length load replay; monitor queue_length, token_release events, short-request p99.
If stable at 30 minutes, promote to 25% and run broader traffic replay for 2 hours.
Full hosted rollout next day if no regressions observed.
Dedicated: schedule staggered upgrades per cluster with SRE support; aim to complete within 7 days for high-impact customers.
Private/on-prem: ship patch artifact and coordinate with customer ops; provide rollback script and guidance.
test_plan: Unit tests for admission token lifecycle to assert release on snapshot_invalidate and preempt edge-cases.
Integration test: mixed-length workload harness running against instrumented scheduler with snapshot rotation toggled.
Load test: multi-tenant density test matching customer profiles (tenant_count=480, short:long ratio 10:1) to confirm no starvation.
Chaos test: simulate host maintenance and network partitioning during admission handoff.
Add tracing asserts to e2e nightly to detect regressions early.
comments: 2026-03-02 Miguel Santos: Confirmed reproducer in staging; race occurs when snapshot invalidate executes concurrently with admission_release path. Working on minimal fix that explicitly releases tokens during invalidate.
2026-03-03 Priya Nair (SRE): Canary guidance prepared and alerted impacted Dedicated customers. Observed one Dedicated cluster with repeated p99 spikes; throttled snapshot rotation as planned.
2026-03-05 Miguel Santos: Hotfix landed in PR #8382. Added admission_watchdog and a small refactor to admission bookkeeping to avoid list corruption.
2026-03-06 Tom Williams (PM): Customer success notified customers of temporary config change and upcoming patch rollout; two escalations acknowledged and scheduled for dedicated upgrade windows.
2026-03-08 QA: Integration + chaos tests green on canary. No regressions in throughput under high concurrency; tail latency reduced by ~85% in repro.
2026-03-10 Miguel Santos: Rolling to 25% and preparing full rollout. Leaving this ticket open for Dedicated/Private coordination and final postmortem.
